title: From Data Centers to the Cloud ☁️
description: Evolution of infrastructure and what changed for security teams.

slides.title: The Old World: On‑Premises Data Centres 🏢
slides.content:
## Before the Cloud

- Companies owned **physical servers** in locked rooms.
- Security was **perimeter‑focused**: a firewall around the building, guards, CCTV.
- Everything inside the perimeter was "trusted" – the **castle‑and‑moat** model.
- Scaling meant buying, racking, and cabling new hardware (weeks of work).

*The castle walls were solid, but once inside, attackers roamed freely.*

quizData.question: The traditional data centre security model is often called...
quizData.explanation: It’s the castle‑and‑moat approach: hard shell, soft interior.

slides.title: Enter the Cloud ☁️
slides.content:
## Virtualisation Changes Everything

- Providers (AWS, Azure, GCP) build **massive shared data centres** and rent out virtual chunks.
- You get a **virtual server** (EC2, VM) in minutes, not months.
- The physical perimeter is now **abstract** – you don’t own the building.
- Security shifts to **identity**, **encryption**, and **software‑defined boundaries**.

*The moat is gone; every door must be locked individually.*

slides.title: Key Differences That Impact Security 🆚
slides.content:
| Factor | On‑Premises | Cloud |
|--------|-------------|-------|
| **Ownership** | You own everything | Provider owns physical |
| **Scalability** | Weeks to add capacity | Seconds to auto‑scale |
| **Perimeter** | Firewall + physical | Identity + network segmentation |
| **Visibility** | Full network tap | Logs & API calls |
| **Patching** | Manual, slow | Provider handles some layers |

These shifts demand a new security mindset: **assume breach, verify explicitly**.

quizData.question: In the cloud, you still control the physical security of the data centre.
quizData.explanation: The cloud provider owns and secures the physical facilities; you secure what’s inside your virtual environment.

slides.title: Remember This 💡
slides.content:
## The Shift in One Sentence
*On‑premises, you trust the network. In the cloud, trust nothing and verify everything.*
